input_signals.name: Equity-Funded Noncash Working Capital
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), LAG(at, 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms issuing equity while accumulating unusually large noncash operating working capital subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: The accrual channel measures growth in current operating assets net of cash and nondebt current liabilities, focusing on where financing proceeds are absorbed rather than reproducing total accruals. Continuous industry-relative issuance weighting avoids the zero mass created by an issuer indicator and should provide a more stable cross-sectional sort.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Working-Capital Rollover Mismatch
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1)), MIN(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(dlc, at), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(dltt, at), 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Noncash working-capital expansion combined with migration from long-term to short-term debt predicts underperformance.
input_signals.reasoning: Expanding illiquid operating working capital while debt maturities shorten creates a direct funding-duration mismatch and raises rollover pressure. This combines the strongest accrual measurement with the successful maturity-compression mechanism, requiring both short-term debt growth and long-term debt contraction.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ), min( ind_rank( delta( ratio( dlc, at ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( dltt, at ), 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Operating-Liability Debt Stack
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(lct, dlc), 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltis, dltr), LAG(at, 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that increase nondebt current liabilities while also issuing net long-term debt subsequently earn lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Growth in current liabilities excluding short-term debt captures greater reliance on deferred supplier, tax, and other operating payments, which can temporarily support operating cash flow. Stacking this implicit creditor financing with explicit net borrowing indicates liquidity pressure rather than the previously tested use of debt to fund operating assets.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( sub( lct, dlc ), 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( dltis, dltr ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Dilution-Funded Working Capital Opacity
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1)), IND_RANK(SUB(IND_RANK(WINSOR(GROWTH(csho, 1), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Noncash working-capital expansion combined with share-count growth unsupported by cash equity proceeds predicts lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The interaction targets stock-financed acquisitions, equity compensation, and other noncash dilution accompanied by balance-sheet accrual growth. These transactions create purchase-accounting and working-capital estimation discretion, linking the two previously successful channels through a specific acquisition-opacity mechanism.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( sub( ind_rank( winsor( growth( csho, 1 ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Working-Capital Financing Absorption
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), DELTA(che, 1)), LAG(at, 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Abnormal working-capital accruals combined with external financing that is not retained as cash predict lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The earlier hard three-way cash-squeeze intersection generated strong portfolio alpha but no linear Fama-MacBeth evidence, suggesting an overly concentrated tail. This continuous financing-absorption channel preserves the use-of-proceeds mechanism while producing a smoother ordering across firms.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), delta( che, 1 ) ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Backed Maturity Extension
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ib), at)), MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(dlc, at), 1))), IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(dltt, at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with cash-backed earnings that replace short-term debt with long-term financing subsequently outperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Operating cash flow exceeding income indicates conservative earnings quality, while declining current debt and increasing long-term debt reduce rollover exposure. The joint state represents credible balance-sheet repair rather than simply reversing an adverse accrual signal or rewarding generic debt issuance.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( sub( oancf, ib ), at ) ), min( ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( dlc, at ), 1 ) ) ), ind_rank( delta( ratio( dltt, at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Chronic Working-Capital Maturity Trap
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(MA(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1), 3)), IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(dlc, dltt), at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent noncash working-capital accruals combined with sustained debt-maturity shortening predict lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: One-period working-capital expansion and maturity compression produced the strongest prior joint evidence, while persistent maturity shortening generated reliable portfolio alpha but a weak slope. Smoothing the working-capital state and measuring a financing trend target a chronic duration mismatch rather than a transitory debt reclassification.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ma( winsor( ratio( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( trend( ratio( sub( dlc, dltt ), at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Noncash Equity Working-Capital Expansion
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(ib, dvc))), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms combining abnormal working-capital accruals with common-equity growth unexplained by cash issuance and retained income subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Equity growth beyond net cash issuance plus income less dividends can reflect stock-financed acquisitions, compensation, or dirty-surplus adjustments. This provides a split-robust alternative to share-count growth and links noncash equity creation to the working-capital estimation discretion often created by acquisitions.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( ib, dvc ) ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Financed Phantom-Earnings Absorption
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(ib, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(NEG(oancf), at))), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(dltis, dltr)), DELTA(che, 1)), LAG(at, 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms reporting high profits despite operating cash burn underperform when externally raised funds are not retained as cash.
input_signals.reasoning: The first component captures the profit-cash contradiction, while the financing-absorption term measures external funds consumed outside the cash account. Multiplying two continuous severity measures avoids the unstable ordering of a triple-MIN intersection while retaining the requirement that both accounting and financing stress be present.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( ind_rank( ratio( ib, at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( neg( oancf ), at ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( dltis, dltr ) ), delta( che, 1 ) ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose noncash working capital and short-term debt both expand despite net equity issuance subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Equity issuance should normally relieve near-term funding pressure, so simultaneous current-debt growth indicates that proceeds are being absorbed rather than strengthening liquidity. Abnormal working-capital accruals identify a specific destination for that financing and a channel through which reported operating strength may be overstated.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ), min( ind_rank( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), lag( at, 1 ) ) ), ind_rank( delta( ratio( dlc, at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(ib, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(NEG(oancf), at))), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(ib, dvc))), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms reporting profits despite operating cash burn underperform when book-equity growth also exceeds cash equity contributions and retained income.
input_signals.reasoning: The equity residual captures noncash capital creation associated with stock-financed acquisitions, compensation, or dirty-surplus adjustments. Its interaction with the profit-cash contradiction targets firms where both earnings and equity expansion rely heavily on noncash accounting channels.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( ind_rank( ratio( ib, at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( neg( oancf ), at ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( ib, dvc ) ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Working-Capital Debt Roll-Forward Absorption
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(dltis, dltr), DELTA(dltt, 1)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Abnormal working-capital accruals combined with long-term borrowing proceeds not retained in long-term debt balances predict lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Net borrowing that exceeds the increase in long-term debt can reflect refinancing absorption, maturity reclassification, or rapid use of financing proceeds. Pairing that directional flow-stock gap with working-capital expansion tests whether borrowed funds are being consumed by operating balance-sheet needs rather than productive, durable financing.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( sub( sub( act, che ), sub( lct, dlc ) ), 1 ), lag( at, 1 ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( sub( dltis, dltr ), delta( dltt, 1 ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.hypothesis: Firms combining net debt issuance with common-equity growth unexplained by cash stock issuance and retained income subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Positive noncash equity expansion can reflect stock-financed acquisitions, compensation, or dirty-surplus adjustments, while net borrowing adds a separate financing layer. Their interaction identifies complex debt-and-noncash-equity expansion rather than merely reversing a clean-surplus shortfall signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( ib, dvc ) ) ), at ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( dltis, dltr ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Working-Capital Debt-Leakage Cash Drain

input_signals.hypothesis: Abnormal working-capital accruals predict lower returns when long-term borrowing is not retained in debt balances and cash is simultaneously depleted.
input_signals.reasoning: The debt roll-forward interaction had strong cross-sectional evidence but weak portfolio alpha, consistent with benign refinancing contaminating its extreme portfolio. Requiring cash depletion isolates cases where the flow-stock gap reflects financing absorption or rollover pressure rather than harmless reclassification.

input_signals.name: Noncash Equity Debt Absorption
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), ADD(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(ib, dvc))), at), 1)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(dltis, dltr), DELTA(che, 1)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms combining noncash equity expansion with net debt financing that is not retained as cash subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Net debt issuance alone produced wrong-signed portfolio evidence when paired with noncash equity expansion, consistent with productive acquisitions contaminating the adverse tail. Subtracting cash accumulation focuses on debt proceeds immediately absorbed by acquisitions, restructuring, or operating needs.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), add( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( ib, dvc ) ) ), at ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( sub( dltis, dltr ), delta( che, 1 ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.reasoning: The archive found adverse evidence for both signs of the equity residual, suggesting that reconciliation difficulty may matter more than its direction. Pairing residual magnitude with working-capital accruals targets firms exhibiting opacity in both operating balance-sheet estimates and common-equity accounting.

input_signals.reasoning: The financing condition now separately requires high net equity issuance and high liquidity deterioration, so nonissuers with falling cash and rising short-term debt cannot generate the strongest signal values. input_signals.reasoning: High gross borrowing and repayment identify rollover dependence that net debt issuance can hide. When funds remain persistently locked in noncash working capital, repeated refinancing is more likely to reflect weak internal cash generation and creditor dependence.
